title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-18
content:
Summary:
- Scratchpad for the intermittent KV-cache/attention-kernel selection bug that appears at certain sequence length transitions (notably around 512->513 and 1024->1025).
- Repro is flaky in CI but more likely on NVidia A100 at driver 525.x and with flash_attn enabled.

Context / hypothesis:
- Observed failures when incoming request has prefix_len (cached tokens) > kernel-dependent threshold. Suspect kernel-specific assumptions about contiguous KV buffers and offsets.
- Two kernels in play: flash_attn (fast, requires packed KV layout) and math_dot (fallback, more permissive). Kernel selection policy switches at runtime depending on sequence length and batch composition.
- Hypothesis A: when we keep KV cache as separate chunks per request and then coalesce, the indexing math differs between kernels leading to out-of-range writes for flash_attn.
- Hypothesis B: quantization (int8/4) kernel path uses different stride assumptions causing shape mismatch.

Repro notes (commands I ran locally on a small repro harness):
- envs tried: ATTENTION_KERNEL=auto | flash_attn | math_dot; KV_CACHE_MODE=chunked | unified; USE_QUANT=1|0
- baseline run (works): 
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python tools/repro_seqlen.py --model gpt-neox-20b --seq 512 --prev 512 --kernel auto --kv-mode unified
- failing run (repro intermittently): 
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python tools/repro_seqlen.py --model gpt-neox-20b --seq 513 --prev 513 --kernel flash_attn --kv-mode chunked  
- force-fallback (temporary workaround, passes): 
  ATTENTION_KERNEL=math_dot CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python tools/repro_seqlen.py --model gpt-neox-20b --seq 513 --prev 513 --kv-mode chunked

Errors / snippets captured:
- Python traceback (trimmed):
  File "serving_runtime/inference.py", line 832, in forward_step
    kv.write_slice(batch_idx, offset, k_chunk)
  File "serving_runtime/kv_cache.py", line 214, in write_slice
    dest[offset:offset+len(k_chunk)] = k_chunk
IndexError: slice assignment index out of range

- C++ runtime log around the moment:
  [2025-11-08 14:12:23.912] WARN attention_kernel_selector: switching to flash_attn (seqlen=513, cached=513)
  [2025-11-08 14:12:23.917] ERROR kv_cache: write_overflow detected shard=2 offset=523264 requested_end=523776 capacity=523520
  [2025-11-08 14:12:23.918] FATAL runtime: aborting request id=abc-123 due to kv cache overflow

- Profiling traces:
  - When kernel=flash_attn: large memcpy at step N (size ~256KB) followed by immediate overflow on next write.
  - When kernel=math_dot: writes are smaller and incremental, no overflow.

What I think is happening:
- Kernel selection changes the expected layout/stride of KV slices (e.g., packed vs unpacked). The KV cache allocation is sized for the worst-case per-request predicted layout, but when the selector switches, the write offsets are computed under the assumption of the previously chosen layout. Race condition in selector + async batching path.
- Another angle: prefix_len accounting bug - we use int32 token counts in Python but int16 in C++ kernel code path for flash_attn causing integer wrap/incorrect offset when accumulated tokens > 65535 (haven't reproduced that threshold yet).

Experiments and results (short log):
- 2025-11-03: force kernel=flash_attn, KV unified -> PASS on 20/20 runs
- 2025-11-04: kernel=auto (selector enabled), KV chunked -> FAIL 3/20 (IndexError slice assignment)
- 2025-11-05: kernel=flash_attn, KV chunked -> FAIL 6/20 (consistent with chunked layout + flash_attn)
- 2025-11-07: kernel=math_dot, KV chunked -> PASS 20/20
- 2025-11-08: added a debug assert in kv_cache writing to log computed offsets -> logs show intermittent negative delta between computed_end and capacity (i.e., computed_end > capacity)

Important code paths touched:
- serving_runtime/kv_cache.py: write_slice, coalesce_chunk, allocate_shard
- serving_runtime/attention_selector.cc: select_kernel_for_batch
- serving_runtime/native/flash_attn_adapter.cu: expects packed KV with stride = head_dim/4 (quantized path)

Quick patches I tried (and results):
- Add defensive clamp in write_slice: if end > capacity -> expand shard (slow) -> makes test pass but hides underlying bug. Not acceptable long-term.
- Force unified KV allocation on request start (allocate enough contiguous space for worst-case) -> eliminates failures but doubles memory for some workloads. Works as a mitigation.
- Add sequence-length-based selector hysteresis (avoid switching kernel mid-batch) -> reduced failure rate but still saw edge-case when batches had mixed prev lengths and async writes overlapped.
- Asserted that token counters use int64 across Python/C++ boundary -> no immediate change to failure rate (but safer).

Next steps / TODOs:
- Reproduce minimal C++/CUDA repro that exercises write_slice + kernel switch without full runtime (lighter harness). Target date: 2025-11-14. Owner: Alex.
- Add stronger invariant checks: track per-shard allocated_bytes vs written_bytes under atomic ops to detect races.
- Audit attention kernel adapters (flash_attn_adapter.cu) for stride/shape assumptions; add explicit comments and precondition checks. Owner: Priya.
- Add end-to-end test in CI that exercises seqlen transitions around 512/1024 with both KV modes and kernel=auto. Mark flaky test as quarantined if unstable. Owner: Marco.
- Follow up GitHub PR: see linked PR #678 (contains initial debug logs and micro repro harness).

Notes to self:
- Check NV driver versions on infra pool used by CI (A100-525.x vs 530.x) — older driver might interact with cudaMemcpy sizing but unlikely.
- Look into whether quantized path (UseQuant=1) changes per-head stride calculation. I saw one crash only when quant enabled.
- Slack thread has more scattered data points from SRE during incident (link above).

Candidate long-term fixes:
- Make kernel selection deterministic per-batch at enqueue time (tag requests with kernel choice) and enforce same kernel during execution. This would remove async switching races.
- Normalize KV layout API so adapters must implement pack/unpack helpers and always accept a standard canonical layout (or request a re-pack before write).
- Add telemetry counters for "kernel_switch_during_batch" and "kv_write_overflow" so we can correlate with customer incidents.

If I get a clean minimal repro, next action is to open a proper bug report (INF-1234) with reproducer, stack traces, and suggested patch to attention_selector. For now, mitigation in prod: force math_dot for seqlen > 512 for affected model family until fix landed (config rollout planned).

Random observables (notes):
- Often fails when batch contains mixing of in-context generation requests where some have 0 prefix and some have large prefix; uneven KV packing may be the trigger.
- Edgecase observed only for models with many heads (>= 32) and head_dim multiple-of-64.

Scratch TODO (quick commands to run locally):
- python tools/repro_seqlen.py --model gpt-neox-20b --seq 1025 --prev 1024 --kernel auto --kv-mode chunked --log-level debug > /tmp/seqlen1025.log 2>&1 &
- gdb --args python tools/repro_seqlen.py ... (attach if see IndexError)
- run small C++ harness: build/kv_harness --kernel flash_attn --seq 513 --prev 513 --mode chunked

End.
